newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trygg-Hansa H1 investment returns strong.
newsitem.headline: Trygg-Hansa H1 investment returns strong.

text.p: Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa on Tuesday posted a 42 percent lift in pre-tax profit for the first half of 1997 which it attributed partly to a robust return on investments.
Trygg-Hansa posted a six month pre-tax profit of 2.13 billion crowns ($265.9 million), above the market consensus forecast of 1.94 billion.

"Our successful venture in the expanding life insurance and savings market continues and the strong investment returns have contributed to further improvement in Trygg-Hansa's financial strength," chief executive Lars Thunell said in a statement.

The company said it saw a sharp increase in volumes in the life and savings market in the six months ending June 30. Business volume, calculated as the sum of life and non-life insurance premiums, savings in investment funds and deposits with Trygg-Banken rose by about 20 percent from a year ago to 1.57 billion crowns.
Shareholders' funds amount to 11.34 billion crowns on June 30 which corresponded to 137 crowns a share.
Trygg-Hansa said the market trend for life insurance and savings had been favourable.
During the first six months its portfolio of life insurance and savings business increased by 15 percent to 134.61 billion crowns.
The combined result for these operations was 163 million crowns compared to 25 million at the same period in 1996.
Its non-life insurance operations came under continued strong rate pressure, with premium volumes continuing to decline, primarily for commerical insurance.
There was a turnaround for personal motor insurance however in the first half with the number of policies up 50 percent.
But the balance on the technical account for non-life insurance business fell to 170 million crowns from 367 million crowns a year ago. Net premiums slipped to 2.46 billion crowns from 2.54 billion.
The number of major claims has risen this year with theft and burglary, particularly in the car segment a contributing factor as was a number of fires at sports facilities.
An anonymous Swedish group has claimed responsibility for about eight fires at sports venues around Stockholm to protest about the city's bid to host the 2004 Olympic Games.

Trygg-Hansa said its asset management activities also performed well in the first half due to rising share prices. The combined value of investments at the half year mark was 153 billion crowns compared to 127 billion a year ago.
The insurer said the total investment return for the Trygg-Hansa Insurance Co Ltd group was 2.23 billion crowns in the six months against 1.82 billion crowns a year earlier.

Trygg-Hansa said a 2.0 billion crowns redemption of 13.14 million B-series shares, announced in May, was expected to be completed around September 24 this year, at which time payment would be made for submitted shares. The share are being redeemed at 152.23 crowns each.
Trygg-Hansa shares were down 3.0 crowns to 170 by 1250 GMT.
-- Belinda Goldsmith, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1045 ($ = 8.01 Swedish Crowns)
